decisions.title: Raises the global rate limit tenfold, from 60 to 600 requests per minute
decisions.whyItMatters: This change affects every endpoint, not just receipts, and the description does not mention it. A reviewer should confirm the increase is intended, since it weakens abuse and brute-force throttling for the whole API.

decisions.title: Stores receipts in an unbounded, process-local in-memory Map instead of the configured Redis cache
decisions.whyItMatters: Entries are never evicted, so memory grows with every distinct order rendered. Each instance keeps its own copy, so the cache is not shared and does not use the cache.driver: redis setting already in config.

decisions.title: Hard-codes the one-hour receipt TTL in code, although config adds a configurable receipts TTL
decisions.whyItMatters: The config value cache.ttlSeconds.receipts (3600) is never read, so changing it has no effect. The ticket explicitly requires the cache lifetime to be configurable.

decisions.title: Serves cached receipts without invalidation when the order changes
decisions.whyItMatters: The cache is keyed only by order.id and is not cleared when items or prices change. A customer can keep downloading a stale receipt for up to an hour after the order is modified.

decisions.title: Adds a receipts config block (currency, footer) that the rendering code never reads
decisions.whyItMatters: Operators may believe they can change the receipt currency or footer here, but the output hardcodes neither. Either wire these settings into renderReceipt or drop them to avoid confusion.

decisions.title: Interpolates raw item names into the plain-text receipt without sanitizing them
decisions.whyItMatters: An item name containing newlines could forge extra receipt lines or a fake total. The impact is limited because the response is text/plain, but it is worth a deliberate decision.
